sample_unit: submitted models (19 continuous-outcome, 12 binary-outcome) from challenge teams
models_evaluated: general linear reference model (SUV and TMTV)
logistic regression reference model (SUV and TMTV)

links.outcome: External-validation performance of radiomics ML models versus simple SUV and TMTV reference models for PFS prediction
links.effect: 6 of 19 continuous-outcome models performed similarly to the simple linear reference model; 1 of 12 binary-outcome models had higher but nonsignificant C-index than the simple logistic regression.
links.quote: This suggests that, for the challenge dataset, there was limited or no value seen from the addition of sophisticated radiomic features and use of machine learning when developing models for outcome prediction.

links.outcome: Whether complex radiomics ML models outperform simple regression models on the same prediction task
links.effect: Some models showed better FOMs than simple linear or logistic regression using SUV and TMTV, but differences were nonsignificant, indicating limited or no added value from complexity.
links.quote: This suggests that, for the challenge dataset, there was limited or no value seen from the addition of sophisticated radiomic features and use of machine learning when developing models for outcome prediction.

unlisted_practices: Community challenge/competition with external test set to compare predictive model solutions

screen.reason: This is a summary report of a multi-team competitive benchmark challenge evaluating ML and radiomics models for predicting progression-free survival in lymphoma compared to standard baseline predictors.
